title: NASA Bennu samples reveal Jupiter's role in mixing inner and outer Solar System material
content: Tiny samples from asteroid Bennu are reshaping scientific understanding of the Solar System’s formation. New evidence indicates that Bennu originated in a region where material from the inner and outer Solar System mixed, with Jupiter playing a surprising role in shaping its formation.
summary: Samples from asteroid Bennu provide new evidence that the asteroid formed where material from the inner and outer Solar System mixed. Jupiter played a surprising role in shaping this formation process.
author: Science Daily

title: Hidden Bias in Human Language Challenges 70 Years of Scientific Assumptions
content: A new study analyzing billions of word uses challenges seven decades of linguistic assumptions. Researchers found that meaning is organized around power, danger, and order, rather than emotion alone. The analysis also revealed a hidden preference for safety in human language, suggesting that word usage may reflect ancient survival instincts.
summary: A groundbreaking study challenges 70 years of assumptions about how human language works. By analyzing billions of word uses, scientists discovered that meaning is organized around power, danger, and order rather than emotion alone, and that human language shows a powerful hidden preference for safety that may reflect ancient survival instincts.
author: Science Daily

content: A personalized mRNA vaccine, tailored to individual patient tumors, has been shown to reduce the risk of melanoma recurrence by more than 40 percent. These findings from a Phase 3 trial highlight the potential of mRNA technology in cancer treatment.
summary: A new personalized mRNA vaccine reduces the risk of melanoma recurrence by over 40 percent. Results from the Phase 3 trial demonstrate the potential of mRNA vaccines in cancer treatment.

title: Lee Chang Dong's Seventh Film 'Possible Love' Addresses 2009 Korean Labor Crisis
content:
Lee Chang Dong’s seventh feature film, Possible Love, draws on true events from 2009 when a Korean conglomerate dismissed a third of its workforce—2,600 employees—after which many of those laid‑off workers died by suicide. The film continues Lee’s long tradition of addressing themes of class, labor, religion, and compressed modernity, portraying a uniquely Korean affliction without a didactic tone.

Possible Love opens with the epigraph “Thou shall not covet.” It follows its characters in the aftermath of the layoffs, depicting a murkier period that resists easy understanding.
summary: Lee Chang Dong's seventh feature film, Possible Love, is inspired by the 2009 Korean conglomerate layoffs that fired 2,600 employees, many of whom later died by suicide. The film examines the aftermath of that labor crisis, continuing Lee's exploration of class, labor, religion, and modernity.

title: Lenovo Yoga 9n offers features that could inform a rumored touchscreen MacBook
content:
The Verge’s Antonio G. Di Benedetto has shared his impressions of the Lenovo Yoga 9n, a 2-in-1 workstation laptop, following its use in testing Nvidia’s RTX Spark platform. As the long-rumored touchscreen MacBook approaches a potential announcement next week, the author suggests that Apple could learn from the Yoga 9n’s design. The Lenovo device is described as a 16-inch convertible with a stylus, which the author finds more enjoyable than other RTX Spark laptops that feature conventional clamshell designs.

The comparison highlights that the RTX Spark processor, like Apple silicon in modern MacBook Pros, is an Arm-based chip with a powerful integrated GPU and substantial unified memory. While other Nvidia-powered laptops also include touchscreens, the Yoga 9n’s 2-in-1 form factor distinguishes it as the most entertaining option in the current lineup. The article posits that this specific combination of hardware and convertible design represents a model for what a future touchscreen MacBook might need to be successful.
summary: Lenovo Yoga 9n offers features that could inform a rumored touchscreen MacBook.

title: Barnes Ice Cap shows Laurentide Ice Sheet may have re-expanded 2,000 years ago
content:
The Barnes Ice Cap on Baffin Island is the last surviving fragment of the Laurentide Ice Sheet, the largest Pleistocene ice sheet that once covered most of Canada under two miles of ice.  A recent study published in Science shows that the Laurentide reached its smallest extent about 3,600 years ago and then began to re‑expand roughly 2,000 years ago.  The researchers interpret this re‑expansion as the initial phase of a new glaciation that continued until around 1960, when human‑caused climate warming halted the growth.

Nicolás Young, a geologist at Columbia University’s Lamont‑Doherty Earth Observatory and the study’s lead author, explains that Barnes is the remaining core of one of the Laurentide domes.  As the dome thinned during the Holocene, its margin retreated onto Baffin Island, leaving the present‑day deflated core that was once two miles thick.

Young notes that Barnes can provide evidence of its own history because the temperature at its base records the ice sheet’s changes.  The cap’s preserved record therefore offers a direct physical link to the Laurentide’s past dynamics.
summary: Barnes Ice Cap sits on the central plateau of Baffin Island, in the Canadian Arctic. It is the last surviving fragment of the Laurentide Ice Sheet, the largest of the Pleistocene ice sheets, which at its peak buried most of Canada under two miles of ice and locked away around 80 meters of sea level.
author: Ars Technica

title: Mars' 1,000-mile cloud modeled, suggests exotic physics
content:
A thin, elongated cloud appears each morning during Martian spring and summer near the volcano Arsia Mons. The wispy formation stretches gradually, reaching over 1,000 miles—roughly the distance from New York to Kansas City—before it dissipates. This cycle repeats for several months, and the cloud was first recorded by a probe in 2018. Scientists have been unable to explain its existence, and the cloud is commonly referred to as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC).

Recently, researchers at Paris’ Sorbonne Université modeled the cloud’s formation for the first time. Their simulations required the inclusion of exotic physics that, while covered in textbooks, is usually regarded as theoretical and has not been directly observed in any planet’s atmosphere. According to lead author Jorge Hernández‑Bernal in a press release, “Once we included this physics in our simulations, the AMEC emerged just as we hoped.”
summary: Scientists have modeled the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud for the first time, showing it may be driven by exotic physics not previously observed in planetary atmospheres. The study, led by Jorge Hernández-Bernal of Paris’ Sorbonne Université, was published after the cloud was first recorded by a probe in 2018.

title: Historian Andrew Smith says policing cannot replace social reform amid French unrest
content: “You can't police yourself into social cohesion. You can't police yourself into a political future,” explains Andrew Smith, historian of modern France at Queen Mary University of London. He identifies a central paradox confronting the French Republic: the state may possess the means to impose public order, yet lack the political capacity to address the demands and grievances driving mass mobilisation. Smith examines the tensions between social protest, presidential authority and democratic legitimacy amid renewed unrest in France: “500,000 people on the streets of France doesn't happen by chance.”
summary: “You can't police yourself into social cohesion. You can't police yourself into a political future,” explains Andrew Smith, historian of modern France at Queen Mary University of London.

title: Paris protest begins at Porte d'Italie after last‑minute route change
content:
A protest began at Paris’s Porte d’Italie after organizers announced a last‑minute change to the march route. The demonstration is part of a series of cost‑of‑living protests taking place across France.

Authorities have deployed additional police nationwide to avoid a repeat of the violence that followed last Saturday’s demonstrations. In Lyon, where protests were banned, police used tear gas to disperse about 150 demonstrators. Government figures say more than half a million people took part in the previous weekend’s actions, and officials expect similarly large crowds today. The movement originated from high‑school students protesting poor conditions and a lack of resources, prompting cities to increase security measures.

In Paris, the Louvre, the Musée d’Orsay and the Picasso Museum are closed, and many luxury boutiques have shut their doors and boarded up windows after looting reported last weekend. France 24 journalist Elitsa Gadeva reports the latest.
summary: A protest in Paris started at the Porte d'Italie after a last‑minute change to the planned route. Extra police have been deployed nationwide as museums and luxury boutiques in Paris remain closed following recent looting.
author: France 24

title: French President Macron condemns racist terrorist attack in Paris suburbs
content:
Authorities are investigating a shooting in the Paris suburbs of Trappes and La Verrière as a potentially racist and Islamophobic terrorist attack. The incident left one person dead and five wounded, including a 12‑year‑old girl who was shot eight times.

Police arrested the suspected gunman, and investigators found three gas cylinders rigged to a timer in his apartment and a submachine gun in his car. The French president condemned the attack, while the mayor of Saint‑Denis denounced the impact of hate speech.

content:
François Picard and Selina Sykes welcomed New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara as the National Football League prepares to expand its international presence to Paris, France. In the meeting, Kamara described the upcoming Saints‑Pittsburgh Steelers game as “an opportunity unlike any other,” noting that it reflects his career achievements and the broader reach of American football.

Kamara also shared personal aspirations, expressing interest in representing his country in flag football at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics. title: Medical experts shocked by Tennessee team’s ‘malpractice’ in Christa Pike’s failed execution
content:
Medical experts have said the Tennessee execution team’s handling of Christa Pike’s lethal‑injection attempt would constitute medical malpractice in a typical clinical setting. The experts’ reaction follows newly released details describing how the state’s intravenous (IV) team spent nearly an hour trying to establish a line in Pike’s arm for the administration of a fatal dose of pentobarbital, a sedative that is normally lethal.

The account of the failed execution was provided in legal filings by Pike’s lawyer, Randy Spivey, who was present inside the death chamber on 30 September when the attempt took place. The documentation, made public on Thursday, outlines the prolonged struggle of the IV team and the resulting survival of Pike after the dose was administered.
summary: Medical experts shocked by Tennessee team’s ‘malpractice’ in Christa Pike’s failed execution.

title: ICC deputy prosecutor says court making progress despite US sanctions
content: Nazhat Shameem Khan claims some staff are facing ‘banking difficulties’ but their work is unaffected The deputy prosecutor of the international criminal court has said new US sanctions are beginning to take effect on its staff but insisted they have not hindered the court’s work. The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, announced the sanctions this month, accusing the ICC – a frequent target of the Trump administration – of being a “rogue court” and declaring: “Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC.”
summary: ICC deputy prosecutor Nazhat Shameem Khan said some staff face banking difficulties from new US sanctions but the court’s work remains unaffected. title: Epstein scandal may recede in midterms, but experts say it remains a voter issue
content:
As U.S. voters head to the polls for the midterm elections, survivors’ advocates in the Jeffrey Epstein investigation have warned that the scandal could recede into the background as other voter concerns dominate. Political experts, however, say the Epstein issue is not disappearing permanently and expect renewed focus on the late financier’s activities when Congress returns.

The experts note that many voters are able to balance day‑to‑day issues such as affordability and artificial intelligence with the ongoing scandal involving the accused sex trafficker whose social circle spanned America’s elite.
summary: Some survivors’ advocates in the Jeffrey Epstein investigation say the scandal could recede into the background as US voters head to the midterm elections. Political experts say the Epstein issue is not going away permanently and voters will balance it with day‑to‑day concerns such as affordability and AI.
author: Guardian World

title: US health authorities add 178 measles cases, total 4,588 across 43 outbreaks
content:
The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported 4,588 measles cases nationwide, more than double the tally in 2025. Federal health authorities added 178 cases this week, and the vaccine‑preventable illness continues across at least 43 outbreaks.

The new data were released as experts criticize the agency for a lack of transparency, and as health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr takes steps to further upend US vaccine infrastructure.
summary: Federal health authorities reported an additional 178 measles cases in the US this week, bringing the CDC's total to 4,588 cases across at least 43 outbreaks. content: Scotland Yard confirmed that it handed a letter to the Duchess of Sussex in 2019 that detailed “alleged offending” involving her father, Thomas Markle Sr. The police said the letter, which they received in January 2019, contained a number of allegations about offences committed outside Britain. title: Israeli soldiers raze Hebron neighbourhood, evicting about 1,500 families
content:
Israeli troops have leveled a neighbourhood in Hebron, driving out hundreds of families as a collective punishment response to a militant attack on an army checkpoint outside the West Bank city, local Palestinian authorities said. The Hebron municipality estimated that 35 hectares (86 acres) had been destroyed or marked for destruction, and about 1,500 people were evicted from their homes by Saturday afternoon in the district of Ein Deir Baha.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu vowed “to destroy this place” in retaliation for the attack. The entire city, home to 250,000 residents, was sealed off by checkpoints at every point of entry.
summary: Israeli soldiers raze Hebron neighbourhood, evicting about 1,500 families.
author: Guardian World

title: RM's Art Exhibition Draws Fans to San Francisco's SFMOMA
content:
K-pop star RM, a member of the band BTS, has launched a new art exhibition titled “RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me” at the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art (SFMOMA). The display features more than 100 pieces from RM’s private collection and is co-curated by SFMOMA’s América Castillo and Hyoeun Kim. The exhibition opened in San Francisco earlier this month and has drawn significant attention from fans.

According to reports, the exhibition provided a boost to SFMOMA, which had previously struggled. RM, whose real name is Kim Namjoon, accepted the invitation to host the show while he was serving in the South Korean military two years ago. At the media preview, RM expressed his enthusiasm for the project, stating that a collection built over a long period of time shows a person more honestly than many other things.
summary: RM's Art Exhibition Draws Fans to San Francisco's SFMOMA.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Arteta concerned over Saka's durability as forward faces possible six-week absence
content: Arteta: ‘We need to understand how to manage his load’ Max Dowman could play against Everton on Saturday Mikel Arteta has expressed concern over Bukayo Saka’s robustness after a series of injuries to the forward in the past year and as he awaits further news on how long he will be out for with a thigh issue. Saka is set for an MRI scan after limping off in the 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich in the Champions League, with Arteta revealing the 25-year-old had “quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury”. Saka will definitely miss Saturday’s game against Evertonand, it is understood, Arsenal fear it could be a grade-two tear that could potentially keep him out for up to six weeks.
summary: Mikel Arteta expressed concern over Bukayo Saka's durability after the player limped off during Arsenal's 2-2 draw with Bayern Munich. Saka is set for an MRI scan and could miss up to six weeks due to a potential grade-two thigh tear.

title: Brewers survive chaotic ninth-inning replay drama to beat Rays in World Series opener
content:
The Milwaukee Brewers defeated the Tampa Bay Rays 3-2 in Game 1 of the World Series on Friday night, securing a victory after a dramatic finish. The game featured a chaotic ninth-inning sequence where Tampa Bay’s Liam Hicks grounded into what appeared to be a game-ending double play. However, the call was overturned following a video review, which showed that Brewers shortstop Cooper Pratt’s right foot was slightly off the bag when he attempted to catch a high throw from second baseman Brice Turang.

Following the overturned play, Brewers closer Trevor Megill faced a jam with runners on second and third bases. Megill escaped the situation by striking out Jonny DeLuca, preserving the lead for Milwaukee. The Brewers’ offense was sparked early when Yelich tripled home a run and scored in the first inning. Pitchers Misiorowski and Megill combined to hold off the Rays’ late fightback, ensuring the Brewers claimed the opening game of the series.
summary: Brewers survive chaotic ninth-inning replay drama to beat Rays in World Series opener.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Catherine Breed Becomes First to Swim Entire California Coastline
content:
Catherine Breed, a 33-year-old ultra-endurance swimmer from the San Francisco Bay Area, has become the first person to swim the entire coastline of California, from its northern-most tip to the Mexican border. She completed the journey on a beach in San Diego on Monday, concluding a swim that began nearly four months prior.

Breed’s support team had prepared for encounters with sharks and storms, but they did not anticipate finishing during a year of historic super El Niño weather. Despite these conditions, Breed navigated an unusually volatile Pacific Ocean, dodging hurricanes, wildlife, and eight-foot waves to reach her destination.
summary: Catherine Breed Becomes First to Swim Entire California Coastline.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Older, calmer, but still playing the hits: Mourinho and Madrid primed for clásico
content:
José Mourinho, who first arrived at Camp Nou 30 years ago as Bobby Robson’s translator, is now the Real Madrid manager tasked with beating Barcelona in the upcoming clásico on Sunday.  He has been with Madrid for only three months and has not yet played a clásico.  The manager returns to the stadium where he last visited in 2013 as the most famous manager in football.

Mourinho has previously declared “today, tomorrow and always, Barcelona in my heart,” and said he would only ever go to Real Madrid to destroy them.  He has now been entrusted with attempting to bring about the destruction of Barcelona.  The return to Camp Nou is framed as a nostalgic moment wrapped in the rivalry between the two clubs.
summary: Once Bobby Robson’s translator at the Camp Nou, Mourinho is tasked with bringing down Barcelona on Sunday José Mourinho has done the por que?, the printout and the press conference no-show, and he’s been here only three months. The Real Madrid manager has played the classics without even playing a clásico.

title: Australia defeats England 78-0 in women’s Rugby League World Cup pool match
content:
Australia dominated England in a Pool A match of the women’s Rugby League World Cup, winning 78‑0 at HBF Park in Perth. The Jillaroos scored 15 tries without reply, underscoring the scoreline’s one‑sided nature.  

The result reiterated the gap in athleticism and skill between the hemispheres and echoed last year’s 90‑4 defeat in Las Vegas. England’s women’s team will need to refocus urgently ahead of next week’s encounter with Samoa if they hope to reach the semi‑finals.
summary: The Jillaroos won 78-0 over England in a pool A match at HBF Park in Perth. The 15‑tries‑to‑none score underscored the gulf in athleticism and skill between the hemispheres, echoing last year's 90‑4 defeat in Las Vegas.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England defeats France 82-0, securing Rugby League World Cup semi‑final hopes
content:
England secured a record-breaking 82-0 victory over France in Pool B + C, a result that keeps their Rugby League World Cup semi-final hopes alive. Herbie Farnworth and Dom Young both scored hat-tricks during the match. The decisive win was necessary because the shortened group stage format means a single defeat is near-ruinous for qualification.

Head coach Brian McDermott had previously admitted that England’s chances of qualification were slim following a 30-12 loss to Tonga on the opening weekend. The path to the semi-finals became clear after Samoa defeated Papua New Guinea 64-6 earlier on Saturday. Samoa, who beat France 78-4 in the previous week, currently holds a points differential of plus-132. England now has a points differential of plus-64, meaning the team will not know if this result ultimately secures their advancement until next weekend.
summary: England beat France 82-0 in Pool B + C, with Herbie Farnworth and Dom Young each scoring hat‑tricks. The win gives England a plus‑64 points differential, keeping their Rugby League World Cup semi‑final hopes alive despite a slim qualification chance after a loss to Tonga.
author: Guardian Sport

content:

title: Cognitive surrender: Artificial intelligence’s threat to democracy
content: Wesleyan University computer science professor Sebastian Zimmeck argues that artificial intelligence threatens democratic citizenship by fostering cognitive surrender. summary: Wesleyan University computer science professor Sebastian Zimmeck says artificial intelligence threatens democratic citizenship by encouraging cognitive surrender. He argues that individual critical thinking and robust regulatory oversight are required to protect personal agency.

title: Russia renews election influence tactics as U.S. midterms approach
content: Researchers who track online influence operations report that Kremlin‑backed groups are renewing tactics previously used to sow distrust and discord in U.S. and global elections. These efforts are intensified during the final stretch of the midterm campaign.
summary: Researchers who track online influence operations say Kremlin-backed groups are renewing tactics they've used to sow distrust and discord in previous elections in the U. S.

title: This Decade Lacks a Big-Impact Midterm, Unlike Past Decades
content: The current decade has yet to produce a midterm election with significant impact on Congress or broader national politics. This stands in contrast to every other decade over the past hundred years, each of which has featured at least one such consequential midterm.
summary: This decade has not produced a midterm that made a big difference in Congress or national politics. Every other decade over the past hundred years has produced at least one such midterm.

title: Norfolk couple wins third high court case to protect Catfield Fen wetland
content:
Tim and Geli Harris, who farm 460 acres in the Norfolk Broads, have spent more than a decade fighting to protect Catfield Fen, a rare wetland in the Norfolk Broads. Their persistence has paid off with a hat‑trick of landmark legal victories, culminating in a recent high‑court win this month.

In the latest ruling, Lady Justice Lieven found that Natural England had failed in its statutory duty to protect Catfield Fen from pollution. Nitrates and phosphates washed from arable fields had entered the fen, threatening its ecological integrity.

Catfield Fen is one of the finest examples of calcareous fen in western Europe and is home to 2,500 species, including rarities such as the fen orchid, crested buckler fern, breeding bittern and swallowtail butterflies. The Harris couple’s legal success underscores the importance of holding polluters and regulators accountable for protecting such internationally important habitats.
summary: Norfolk couple wins third high court case to protect Catfield Fen wetland.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Storm Boelo to bring up to 80mph gusts and heavy rain to northern UK
content:
Storm Boelo, the second named storm of the season, is forecast to hit northern parts of the United Kingdom this weekend. Meteorologists predict heavy, frequent showers and winds that could exceed 80 mph, potentially disrupting travel and aggravating existing power outages.

The storm follows Friday’s Storm Austen, after which thousands of residents in the north remain without electricity. Authorities warn that Boelo’s strong winds and heavy rain could cause additional power cuts and further inconvenience for communities already affected by the earlier storm.
summary: Storm Boelo, the second named storm of the season, is expected to bring heavy, frequent showers and winds potentially exceeding 80mph to northern parts of the UK. It follows Friday’s Storm Austen, which left thousands without power, and is expected to disrupt travel and cause additional power cuts in the north.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Trump rule lets Alaska hunters bait bears with doughnuts, bacon
content: Critics decry Trump administration rule that lets hunters lure bears with human foods on federal lands in Alaska A new Trump administration rule allows hunters to bait bears on federal lands in Alaska with bacon, doughnuts, meat scraps or other human foods typically used to help kill the trophy animals at close range. Opponents say the practice will cause bears to be more aggressive around humans, and allege that the rule change is a political gift to largely rightwing trophy hunters. The rule replaces a 2024 Biden administration rule that banned the practice, and environmental groups criticized the move as “indefensible and inexcusable”.
summary: Trump rule lets Alaska hunters bait bears with doughnuts, bacon.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Investigational vaccine generates immune response to KRAS mutations in pancreatic cancer study
content: A randomized phase 2 trial led by Mayo Clinic researchers found that an investigational vaccine enabled the immune system to recognize and respond to KRAS mutations that drive most pancreatic cancers. The results, published in Nature Medicine, are intended to inform the design of a subsequent phase 3 trial.
summary: An investigational vaccine helped the immune system recognize and respond to mutations that drive most pancreatic cancers, according to results from a randomized phase 2 clinical trial led by Mayo Clinic researchers. The findings, published in Nature Medicine, will help researchers design a larger phase 3 clinical trial.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Kenya reports second Ebola death, a 65-year-old relative of first patient
content: Kenya’s Health Ministry announced on Friday that the country’s second Ebola death was a 65‑year‑old woman who was a close relative of the first patient. She died after developing symptoms while in quarantine.
summary: Kenya's Health Ministry announced the country's second Ebola death on Friday. The deceased was a 65-year-old woman, a close relative of the first patient, who died after developing symptoms while in quarantine.

title: NASA aims to build moon base and land astronauts within two years
content: NASA says it is accelerating its lunar program, aiming to construct a moon base and send astronauts back to the lunar surface within as little as two years. The agency emphasizes a rapid pace modeled on the urgency of the Apollo era.
summary: NASA is moving fast on its plans to build a moon base. The agency intends to return astronauts to the lunar surface in as little as two years.
author: Phys.org

title: Typhoon Champi cuts power to thousands of homes in Taiwan
content: Typhoon Champi’s fierce winds knocked out power to thousands of homes in Taiwan. On Saturday, emergency crews scrambled to restore electricity to tens of thousands of residences as the storm continued its path toward China and Japan.
summary: Emergency crews scrambled on Saturday to restore power to tens of thousands of homes in Taiwan after Typhoon Champi's fierce winds battered the island. The storm is moving toward China and Japan.

title: FAU study finds virtual lightsaber swings and punching boost pattern learning in VR
content: New research from Florida Atlantic University’s College of Engineering and Computer Science reports that physically interacting in virtual reality—specifically punching a virtual response box or swinging a virtual lightsaber—can dramatically improve learning on certain pattern‑based tasks. The findings challenge long‑standing assumptions about how people learn.
summary: Researchers at Florida Atlantic University's College of Engineering and Computer Science found that punching a virtual response box or swinging a virtual lightsaber dramatically improves learning on certain pattern‑based tasks in virtual reality. The results challenge long‑standing assumptions about how people learn.
author: Phys.org

title: Astronomers debate nature of tiny red dots seen by James Webb Telescope
content: The James Webb Space Telescope is detecting tiny red dots across the sky. Astronomers have not reached a consensus on the nature of these points, though a subset of researchers suggests they could be massive stars that contain black holes within them.
summary: The Webb telescope sees tiny red dots everywhere. Astronomers disagree on what they are, with some suggesting they are enormous stars containing black holes.

title: WIRED Finds 12 Affordable Mechanical Watches Under $400
content: WIRED and its panel of watch experts hunted for real mechanical timepieces at rock-bottom prices and found a wealth of options. Here are our favorites.
summary: WIRED and its panel of watch experts hunted for real mechanical timepieces at rock‑bottom prices. They found 12 affordable options under $400 and highlighted their favorites.

title: Apple’s folding iPhone Duo sparks indie developers to create quirky apps
content: Apple’s first folding phone, the iPhone Duo, is prompting indie developers to build fun, quirky applications that make use of the device’s dual‑screen layout and hinge mechanism. The article highlights nine distinct apps that users can explore to experience the Duo’s unique capabilities.
summary: Apple’s first folding phone is inspiring indie developers to create fun, quirky apps that take advantage of the screen and hinge. The article highlights nine of these apps for users to try on the Duo.

title: Newport residents oppose new hyperscale datacentre amid AI boom
content:
The new hyperscale data‑centre, standing 23 metres tall on prefabricated panels, has been erected on the western fringes of Newport, South Wales. The structure dominates the view of Dale Johnston, who has opened the gate to his suburban garden to show his grandchildren a trampoline and a slide. Johnston’s wife sits beside him, and the family has chairs set up for their visits. The building’s bulk blocks the autumnal sky that once bathed the area.

Local Labour politicians have promoted the data‑centre as a source of new jobs for the community. Despite this, Johnston feels the loss of the sunlit environment he once enjoyed. He has described the treatment of residents as “disgusting” and expressed frustration over the visual impact the facility has on his neighbourhood.

The situation illustrates the tension between the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure and the concerns of local residents. While the project promises economic benefits, it also brings significant changes to the landscape and quality of life for those living nearby.
summary: A 23‑metre‑high hyperscale datacentre now dominates the western fringe of Newport, South Wales, obscuring sunlight for nearby homes. Labour politicians call the project a job creator, but local residents, including Dale Johnston, say they have been treated poorly and are fighting back.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Rubio urges Cubans seeking change to form discrete partnership with CIA
content:
Former Senator Marco Rubio urged Cubans who want change to establish a “discrete partnership” with the CIA. He said the partnership could help those seeking a new direction in Havana.

The Trump administration has repeatedly stated its goal is to bring about a change in Havana’s leadership. President Donald Trump has claimed the country is “ready to fall.”
summary: Senator Rubio called on Cubans who want change to establish a discreet partnership with the CIA. The Trump administration has repeatedly said its goal is to bring about a change in Havana's leadership, and President Donald Trump has claimed the country is “ready to fall.”

title: Italy Prepares for Saturday Protests Over Cost of Living and Budget Cuts
content: Italy is preparing for a Saturday of protests in eight cities, including Rome and Milan, over budget cuts and the high cost of living. After unrest the previous weekend, authorities said they will deploy heavy security, using drones and helicopters to monitor the marches.
summary: Italy is preparing for a day of protests on Saturday in eight cities, including Rome and Milan, against budget cuts and the high cost of living. Authorities have announced heavy security measures, using drones and helicopters to monitor the marches.

title: Ukraine regains stable Starlink and Starshield connection
content: Ukraine’s defence minister announced on Saturday that the country has restored a “stable” connection to the Starlink and Starshield satellite communications systems. The recent disruptions to the SpaceX‑made network had previously caused tensions with Washington, which the link is described as crucial for Ukrainian army operations.
summary: Ukraine has regained a stable connection to the Starlink and Starshield satellite communications systems, Kyiv's defence minister said on Saturday. Recent disruptions to the connection led to tensions with Washington over the SpaceX‑made network that is crucial to the Ukrainian army's operations.

title: Paris police reroutes authorised trade union march to Place d’Italie–Porte de Vincennes
content:
The Paris police prefecture announced a last‑minute change to the authorised trade union march scheduled for 24 October. The new route will run from Place d’Italie to Porte de Vincennes.

Earlier that morning, many protesters gathered at Place de la Bastille, the march’s original starting point, before the route change was issued. The unexpected shift left participants confused and uncertain about where to proceed.

France 24 journalist Elitsa Gadeva reports the latest developments from the scene.
summary: The Paris police prefecture altered the authorised trade union march route at the last minute before the 24 October mobilisation, setting the new path between Place d’Italie and Porte de Vincennes. Many protesters arrived at the original starting point at Place de la Bastille and were left confused about where to go.
author: France 24

title: Thousands march in Orléans against National Rally congress
content:
France’s far‑right National Rally is holding its annual congress in Orléans, south of Paris. The event is expected to officially launch Marine Le Pen’s presidential campaign and re‑elect Jordan Bardella as party leader. Thousands of supporters are anticipated to attend the rally.

A major counter‑demonstration has been organised to oppose racism, fascism and imperialism. Local authorities are preparing for potential clashes between the National Rally supporters and the counter‑demonstrators.

Antonia Kerrigan reports the latest developments.
summary: France’s far‑right National Rally is holding its annual congress in Orléans, where it is expected to launch Marine Le Pen’s presidential campaign and re‑elect Jordan Bardella as party leader. A major counter‑demonstration against racism, fascism and imperialism is planned, and local authorities are preparing for possible clashes between the groups.
author: France 24

title: French students vow to continue protests despite violence concerns
content: French students have pledged to continue protesting. Across France, both young and older citizens are weighing the risks of joining demonstrations amid growing concerns about violence, according to a report by France 24’s Ophelie Jackson.
summary: French students have pledged to keep protesting. Amid growing concerns over violence, people across France are weighing whether joining demonstrations is worth the risk, according to France 24’s Ophelie Jackson.
author: France 24

title: Typhoon Champi battering Taiwan with 180 km/h winds leaves 56,000 without power
content: Typhoon Champin is moving toward China and Japan after battering Taiwan with heavy rain and winds of up to 180 km/h. The storm left 56,000 households on the island without power, according to reporters Nicolas Chamontin and Ophelie Jacobson.
summary: Typhoon Champi battered Taiwan with heavy rain and winds up to 180 kilometres per hour. The storm left about 56,000 households without power as it moves toward China and Japan, according to reporters Nicolas Chamontin and Ophelie Jacobson.

title: Netanyahu orders cordon of Hebron after attack that killed two Israeli soldiers
content: Israel imposed widespread closures across the occupied West Bank and displaced residents after Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited the attack site near Hebron and instructed security forces to immediately cordon off the city. The developments were reported by Morgan Ayre.
summary: Israel imposed widespread closures across the occupied West Bank and displaced residents after attacks by Palestinian gunmen that killed two Israeli soldiers. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited the site of the attack near Hebron and instructed security forces to immediately cordon off the city.

title: Aaron Rodgers says NFL would cancel Paris game if protests make it unsafe
content: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers said Friday that the NFL would have cancelled its first regular‑season game in Paris if the situation were deemed unsafe because of recent mass protests. The Steelers are set to play the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in Saint‑Denis on Sunday.
summary: Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers said Friday the NFL would cancel its first regular-season game in Paris if recent mass protests made the situation unsafe. The Steelers are scheduled to face the New Orleans Saints at Stade de France in Saint‑Denis on Sunday.

title: Brits stockpile tinned food, loo roll and power banks after three‑day emergency advice
content:
The UK government launched a campaign on Thursday urging citizens to stockpile a three‑day supply of essentials for emergencies.  

Some residents have already begun stockpiling dried foods, bottled water, medicine, and backup power banks in response to official warnings about Russian state‑sponsored terrorism and climate‑related risks.
summary: The UK government launched a campaign on Thursday urging people to set aside three days’ worth of supplies for emergencies. Some residents are already stockpiling dried foods, bottled water, medicine stocks, tinned food, loo roll and backup power banks after official warnings about Russian state‑sponsored terrorism and the climate crisis.
author: Guardian World

title: UK Finance accused of cherry‑picking bank tax data, omitting Paris
content:
A banking lobby group has been criticised for allegedly cherry‑picking data in a report shared with John Healey. Campaigners say the figures, which claim a tax rise for banks in next week’s budget would make London less competitive than rival financial hubs, are misleading because they omit Paris, a major competitor.  

The group, UK Finance – which represents banks such as Lloyds, JP Morgan and Revolut – produces an annual report that adds together corporation tax, social security, VAT and bank‑specific levies to calculate the total taxes paid by a large bank. The criticism focuses on the report’s exclusion of Paris from its competitiveness comparison.
summary: Banking lobby group UK Finance, which represents Lloyds, JP Morgan and Revolut, was accused of cherry‑picking data and misleading the British government. Campaigners say the figures shared with John Healey omit the rival city Paris and claim a tax rise would make London less competitive.
author: Guardian World

title: Chef James Robson signs deal to open Fallow outpost in Gulf amid UK tax surge
content: A leading restaurateur says that Gulf countries actively assist businesses in setting up operations, and that east Asia is noted for a strong work ethic. He adds that some of London’s top restaurants are opening branches in Dubai in response to what he describes as a “tax tsunami” in the UK and a perceived better work ethic abroad. James Robson, co‑owner of Fallow in St James’s Market—described as the capital’s hottest restaurant and serving 1,000 diners a day—has just signed a deal to open an outpost in the Gulf.
summary: Some of London’s top restaurants are opening branches in Dubai because of a “tax tsunami” in the UK and better work ethic abroad, according to a leading restaurateur. James Robson, co‑owner of Fallow in St James’s Market, has signed a deal to open an outpost in the Gulf.
author: Guardian World

title: Irish musician Dónal Lunny dies at 79 from cancer
content: Founding member of Planxty, Lunny went on to play for bands such as Moving Hearts, the Bothy Band and Coolfin The Irish traditional musician Dónal Lunny has died at the age of 79 from cancer. Lunny rose to prominence in the trio Rakes of Kildare alongside his brother Frank and Christy Moore. He went on to play in bands such as Planxty, Moving Hearts, the Bothy Band and Coolfin among others and toured the world.
summary: Dónal Lunny, a 79‑year‑old Irish traditional musician, died after battling cancer. He was a founding member of Planxty and performed with the Rakes of Kildare, Moving Hearts, the Bothy Band and Coolfin.
author: Guardian World

title: Police arrest suspect after fire destroys Hitler's Eagle's Nest in Bavaria
content:
German police have arrested a suspect after a fire ripped through Adolf Hitler’s former mountain retreat in Bavaria, leaving the historic “Eagle’s Nest” largely destroyed.  

Around 200 firefighters were deployed on Friday night to combat the blaze at the Kehlsteinhaus, a purpose‑built, protected residence on the peak of Obersalzberg in the remote southern part of Germany. The fire severely damaged the Nazi meeting place.
summary: German police arrested a suspect after a fire ripped through Adolf Hitler’s former mountain retreat, the Eagle’s Nest, in Bavaria. About 200 firefighters were deployed on Friday night to fight the blaze at the protected Kehlsteinhaus residence on Obersalzberg.
author: Guardian World

title: Protests begin across France, prompting shop, business and tourist site closures
content:
Protests have begun across France, prompting the closure of shops, businesses and tourist sites. French authorities plan to deploy 70,000 police officers nationwide as the demonstrations unfold. Organisers also anticipate parallel protests in Italy, Spain, Austria, Portugal, Albania and Ireland.

Among the participants is Jesse, a 40‑year‑old charity worker from the north of Paris, who joined a street march. Jesse said she is angry and proud to support schoolchildren’s demands for better conditions, emphasizing the need for collective solidarity.
summary: France will deploy 70,000 officers as protests start nationwide, with shops, businesses and tourist sites closed. Demonstrations are also expected in Italy, Spain, Austria, Portugal, Albania and Ireland, and participants such as 40‑year‑old charity worker Jesse from north Paris joined to support schoolchildren’s demands for better conditions.
author: Guardian World

title: Kim Jong-un crosses over newly opened bridge into China
content:
Kim Jong‑un crossed the newly opened New Yalu River Bridge to enter China, marking the North Korean leader’s first known trip abroad in more than a year, South Korean officials said.  

According to a government source quoted by Yonhap on Saturday, the leader arrived in the Chinese border city of Dandong, Liaoning province, after traveling by train from Pyongyang to Sinuiju and then crossing the bridge.  

The visit underscores the renewed use of the bridge for cross‑border travel between North Korea and China.
summary: Kim Jong-un crosses over newly opened bridge into China.
author: Guardian World

title: British mother dies rescuing two sons after current sweeps them off North Bimini
content: A 36‑year‑old British woman died in the Bahamas while attempting to rescue her two sons during a snorkelling outing. A current off North Bimini swept the boys away; they were later rescued, police said. The Royal Bahamas Police Force confirmed the incident occurred on Tuesday and has opened an investigation into the woman’s death. No further details were provided.
summary: A 36-year-old British woman died in the Bahamas while trying to rescue her two sons after a current swept them away while snorkeling off North Bimini. The two boys were later rescued and the Royal Bahamas police force launched an investigation.
author: Guardian World

title: Limoges city hall ruins become symbol of France's split over national protests
content: The ruins of Limoges city hall have become a symbol of France’s division amid national protests. Some younger residents describe the destruction as unfortunate collateral damage in a wider movement, while others label the fire an unacceptable tragedy.
summary: The ruined Limoges city hall is being described as a symbol of a France divided by national protests. Younger residents view the town hall's destruction as unfortunate collateral damage in a broader movement, while others consider the fire an unacceptable tragedy.

title: Zelensky says Starlink limits hurt troops as US officials, Musk dispute control
content: President Zelensky says limits to the technology continue to affect Ukrainian forces. US officials and Elon Musk give conflicting accounts of who controls Ukraine’s access to Starlink.
summary: President Zelensky says limits to the technology continue to affect Ukrainian forces. US officials and Elon Musk offer conflicting accounts of who controls it.
author: BBC World

title: Bill Murray Stars in Travelogue A Course Called Ireland, Declares It’s Not About Golf
content:
A new travelogue, “A Course Called Ireland,” follows author Tom Coyne as he drives around Ireland playing various golf courses with his friend, actor Bill Murray. The series presents the two men teeing off and engaging in drunken pub singalongs, while also showcasing the country’s landscape.

In the show’s opening sequence the producers promise that “This is not a show about golf,” and “It’s not even a show about Bill Murray.” The promise is followed by a scene in which an Irish woman standing by the roadside misidentifies the actor as Bill Cosby, adding a moment of humor to the program.

The reviewer expresses skepticism toward travelogues, noting that they often feature celebrities in contrived situations that present a sentimental postcard of a place. The writer also criticizes the allure of golf for famous people, describing the sport as historically tied to social exclusivity and extensive land ownership, and remarks that the show feels like a strange intersection of interests that he finds unexpectedly entertaining.
summary: Bill Murray appears in the travelogue A Course Called Ireland, which follows author Tom Coyne as they drive around Ireland playing various courses. The show claims it is not about golf or Bill Murray, despite featuring both.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Former Port Adelaide player Daniel Stewart dies at 37
content: Key forward played 36 games and kicked 31 goals between 2010 and 2013 Power will wear black armbands at first home game of 2027 season Former Port Adelaide player Daniel Stewart has died suddenly at the age of 37. The Power confirmed Stewart’s death on Saturday as the club said it was “deeply saddened” by the news that had come as a “shock”.
summary: Former Port Adelaide key forward Daniel Stewart, who played 36 games and kicked 31 goals between 2010 and 2013, died suddenly at age 37. The Power confirmed his death on Saturday and will wear black armbands at the first home game of the 2027 season.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Canada defeats England 31-22, ending Red Roses' decade-long streak of consecutive wins
content:
Canada defeated England 31-22 in Ottawa, marking the Red Roses' first consecutive defeat in ten years. This result represented Canada's third victory against England in their last 74 matches and followed a win the previous Friday that ended England’s unbeaten run. The performance has been described as a formidable message to the rest of world rugby, with some suggesting Canada are serious contenders for the 2029 World Cup trophy. This assessment is based on the rate of their performance improvement over the past year, particularly since their 2025 World Cup final loss to England.

On a cold night in Ottawa, Canada played with freedom and pace to secure the win. Captain Sophie de Goede, the reigning world player of the year, scored a hat-trick and provided excellent defensive work. Julie Omokhuale also stood out during a strong team performance.
summary: Canada beat England 31-22 in Ottawa, giving England their first consecutive loss in ten years. Captain Sophie de Goede scored a hat‑trick and delivered strong defensive play.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Survivors voice concerns over slow change in gymnastics after Nassar scandal
content:
The 2018 conviction of former USA Gymnastics team doctor Larry Nassar has triggered a worldwide reckoning in the sport. A decade after the Indianapolis Star first reported Nassar’s sexual abuse, hundreds of women have come forward with allegations that led to his conviction and imprisonment. Nassar’s case, which also involved his work at Michigan State University, prompted investigations into how gymnastics programs worldwide had allowed predators to abuse young athletes.

The fallout revealed that many countries faced questions about their own failures to protect victims from sexual, physical, and emotional abuse. Despite these revelations, survivors and advocates say progress has been slow. This week, on a large houseboat moored in Rotterdam—just three tram stops from the Ahoy Arena hosting the World Gymnastics Championships—survivors and advocates voiced concerns that the pace of change in gymnastics remains insufficient.
summary: The 2018 conviction of former USA Gymnastics team doctor Larry Nassar triggered a global reckoning in the sport. A decade later, survivors and advocates on a houseboat in Rotterdam, near the Ahoy Arena hosting the World Gymnastics Championships, voiced concerns that the pace of change has been too slow.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Niall Morgan's last kick crowns Edendork first Tyrone Senior Football title
content: Niall Morgan delivered a memorable final kick, scoring a sensational two‑pointer that broke the hearts of Errigal Ciaran. His shot sealed the win for Edendork, crowning them Tyrone Senior Football champions for the first time in history. The moment has been described as a dream fulfilled and a moment that will live forever.
summary: Niall Morgan's sensational two-pointer with the final kick broke Errigal Ciaran hearts. Edendork were crowned Tyrone Senior Football champions for the first time.
author: BBC Sport

title: England lose to Canada 31-22 in second consecutive WXV Global Series match
content: England lost to Canada in Ottawa, falling 31‑22 in their WXV Global Series match. This defeat marked the second consecutive week England was beaten by the Canadians.
summary: England were beaten by Canada 31-22 in a WXV Global Series match in Ottawa. It was England's second loss to Canada in as many weeks.
author: BBC Sport

title: Canada beats England 31-22 in Ottawa, handing England back-to-back losses
content: Canada defeated England 31–22 in Ottawa, handing the English side back‑to‑back losses for the first time in a decade. The Canadian victory featured a hat‑trick from captain Sophie de Goede.

title: DOJ halted evidence sharing on Alex Pretti, Renee Good killings, officials say
content: Minnesota officials told a court, in a filing reviewed by the Associated Press, that the Department of Justice has ceased providing evidence concerning the 2024 shootings of Alex Pretti and Renee Good by immigration officers. The officials say the federal government stopped sharing the evidence related to the two deaths.
summary: Minnesota officials said the Department of Justice has stopped sharing evidence about the killings of Alex Pretti and Renee Good by immigration officers earlier this year. The statement was made in a court filing reviewed by the Associated Press.

title: CBS reports feds knocking on doors to question voters' immigration status
content: CBS reports that federal agents are going door‑to‑door to question voters’ immigration status. The source includes a statement urging protection of eligible Americans’ right to vote without fear and asserting that the administration should rely on policy and persuasion rather than tactics that could intimidate voters.
summary: Federal agents are reportedly going door‑to‑door to question voters’ immigration status, according to CBS. The statement urges protecting eligible Americans’ right to vote without fear and warns that such tactics could deter voting.

title: President Trump to rally in Fort Myers, Florida on Friday
content: President Trump will hold a rally in Fort Myers, Florida, on Friday. Republicans in the state are feeling bullish about statewide races. Fort Myers lies in the 19th Congressional District, where Rep. Byron Donalds (R) vacated his seat to run for governor and is favored to win against Democrat David Jolly.
summary: President Trump will hold a rally in Fort Myers, Florida on Friday. The event occurs as Republicans in the state are feeling bullish about statewide races, including the 19th Congressional District where Rep. Byron Donalds (R) vacated his seat to run for governor and is favored to win against Democrat David Jolly.
author: The Hill

title: Former FBI officials Nikki Floris, Bradley Benavides charged for lying to Congress
content:
Two former FBI officials, Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, have been charged with lying to Congress about their role in the agency’s investigation of Hunter Biden’s laptop. Both served on the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force in 2019 and 2020.

According to a post by FBI Director Kash Patel, Floris and Benavides were taken into custody on Friday. The charges stem from alleged false statements made to congressional investigators regarding their involvement in the laptop probe.
summary: Two former FBI officials, Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, were charged with lying to Congress about their involvement in the agency’s investigation of Hunter Biden’s laptop. Both served on the FBI’s Foreign Influence Task Force in 2019 and 2020 and were taken into custody on Friday, according to FBI Director Kash Patel.
author: The Hill

title: Mary Peltola calls DOJ lawsuit to block Alaska election certification desperate
content: Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola (D) responded to the Justice Department’s (DOJ) lawsuit seeking to block her state from certifying its election results should her Republican challenger lose, saying Friday the move was “frivolous.” “This is clearly corruption. This is clearly a very desperate attempt to cling to power, using his allies in Washington, D. C.…
summary: Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola (D) said the Justice Department's lawsuit seeking to block Alaska from certifying its election results if her Republican challenger loses was frivolous. She called the suit corruption and a desperate attempt by the GOP to cling to power using allies in Washington, D.C.
author: The Hill

title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio offers discreet CIA partnership to Cubans
content: Secretary of State Marco Rubio used a Friday social‑media post to propose a discreet CIA partnership to Cubans. He said “now is the time” for anyone wanting to “create positive change” in the Caribbean nation and urged those disappointed by “failed promises, corruption, and the privileged lives of only a few” to seize the opportunity.
summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio posted on Friday that he is offering Cubans a discreet CIA partnership. He called on those frustrated by failed promises and corruption to seize the chance to create positive change.
author: The Hill

title: DNI Jay Clayton warns Secretary Rubio of advanced Iranian plots to target US officials
content: A declassified intelligence memo dated Friday reports that Iranian plots to target and kill U.S. officials in the Middle East have “substantially increased” and have reached “advanced stages.” The memo, signed by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, was addressed to Secretary of State Marco Rubio and arrived days after the State Department ordered a departure.
summary: DNI Jay Clayton warns Secretary Rubio of advanced Iranian plots to target US officials.
author: The Hill

title: Study identifies overlooked off switch in lung tumors that may limit immunotherapy response
content: New research led by Olga Anczuków, a professor at The Jackson Laboratory for Genomic Medicine in Farmington, Connecticut, and deputy director of the NCI‑designated Jackson Laboratory Cancer Center, has identified an overlooked mechanism in lung‑cancer tumors that may help explain why most patients do not respond to immunotherapy.
summary: An overlooked mechanism in lung cancer tumors may help explain why most patients do not respond to immunotherapy. The finding comes from new research led by Olga Anczuków, a professor at The Jackson Laboratory for Genomic Medicine in Farmington, Connecticut, and deputy director of the NCI‑designated Jackson Laboratory Cancer Center.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Scientists propose national microbiome plan to curb chronic disease
content: Scientists have put forward a national microbiome plan intended to help prevent chronic disease. Rutgers researchers are participating in an international call for a “microbiome moonshot,” a coordinated effort to identify which microorganisms within the human body contribute to chronic illness and how other microbes might be used for tissue repair.
summary: Scientists have proposed a national microbiome plan aimed at preventing chronic disease. Rutgers researchers are part of an international call for a microbiome moonshot to identify disease‑causing microbes and explore therapeutic microbes.

title: Paleolithic DNA shows east‑west connections across Ice Age Europe
content: Scientists have found that people of the Gravettian culture, living in Europe more than 30,000 years ago, were connected across long distances. An international research team led by the University of Vienna uncovered new genetic evidence of these east‑west links. The study, published in Science Advances, combines genomic data from rare human remains with human DNA preserved in cave sediments. content: Climate change is raising flood risk across the U.K., prompting calls for communities to become resilient and “live with water.” Yet in some flood‑prone areas, residents reject this approach, arguing that resilience shifts responsibility from institutions to citizens rather than providing help.

content: Researchers at Lund University in Sweden report that an ancient virus embedded in chimpanzee DNA appears to silence a gene that remains active in humans. The team suggests that a viral pandemic that occurred several million years ago may help explain this divergence.

content:

When meiosis fails in humans, the resulting errors can cause infertility, miscarriage, or birth defects.

content:

content: The Malik Lab, led by HHMI investigator Harmit Malik at the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center, focuses on competition at the genomic level. Rather than human rivalry, the team studies how genomes clash with one another. Their research centers on rapid evolution—genetic changes that occur within a few generations instead of millennia. Malik’s work highlights that these swift shifts are often driven by genetic conflicts, where different genetic elements compete to maximize their own success at the expense of others.

content: Humble breakfast staple at heart of trend stirred up by health concerns and hearty spoonfuls of nostalgia The clocks may be going back in the UK this weekend, but the biggest sign winter is coming is a steaming bowl of porridge on a breakfast table. content:

content:
Data released under freedom of information laws and examined by the Guardian shows that the majority of levelling‑up projects remain incomplete years after funding was allocated. Of the 1,347 projects recorded, 821 had not been finalised as of May 2024. The analysis also found that in 73 council areas where bids were accepted, none of the projects had been fully completed.

content:

title: SpaceX launches 27 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg as Falcon 9 cadence slows
content: SpaceX launched its newest batch of Starlink broadband internet satellites today (Oct. 23) from the California coast. The spacecraft, Starlink Group 15-15, were stacked 27 high inside the payload fairing of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, which lifted off from Pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 6:48 p. M. EDT (2248 GMT; 3:48 p. M. Local time in California). The rocket's first stage booster, designated B1063, executed its main engine cutoff and stage separation about 2.5 minutes into flight, sending the second stage to continue onward to low Earth orbit (LEO). The vehicle's two-piece protective payload fairing was jettisoned just before T+3 minutes. The Falcon 9's first stage, shortly after its drone-ship landing on Oct. 23, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) The booster, meanwhile, reoriented for its descent back to Earth. As the mission clock passed 8 minutes, B1063 began its landing burn, and it touched down about 20 seconds later on SpaceX's droneship "Of Course I Still Love You." This was the 36th launch and landing for B1063, which notably launched NASA's DART asteroid-smashing mission in November 2021. The Falcon 9's upper stage completed its first engine burn shortly after B1063 landed and will coast for about 45 minutes before initiating a second and final orbital insertion burn. Following that burn's execution, deployment of the vehicle's 27 satellites into LEO is scheduled to begin 62 minutes after launch. Previous Booster B1063 launches Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich | DART | Transporter-7 | Iridium OneWeb | SDA-0B | NROL-113 | NROL-167 | NROL-149 | NAOS | 26 Starlink missions Today's Starlink liftoff adds to SpaceX's growing constellation of more than 11,000 active spacecraft. But Starlinks aren't launching quite as often as they used to, as SpaceX shifts its focus from the Falcon 9 to its bigger and more powerful Starship rocket. Starship is designed for full reusability and is equipped with a payload bay outfitted to accommodate SpaceX's upgraded Version 3 Starlink satellites, which are too large for the workhorse Falcon 9. Starship is still under development, but once the rocket begins operational flights (and that day is getting closer), SpaceX plans to phase out the Falcon 9 and its Falcon Heavy variant almost entirely. Falcon 9's 100th launch of 2026 was the Starlink 10-49 group from SpaceX's pad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, which was later revealed to be the final Falcon 9 Starlink mission that would fly from Florida's Space Coast. The same might soon be true for Starlink launches from the West Coast as well. The reduction in missions lifting off from Florida has slowed Falcon 9's Starlink launch cadence considerably. At their peak, these missions were flying every two to three days. But the most recent one before today lifted off 11 days ago, and that launch itself was the first Starlink mission in more than three weeks. Today's launch was the 116th Falcon 9 flight so far in 2026, with about three-quarters of those being dedicated to Starlink. The reduced cadence will likely solidify 2025 as the Falcon 9's busiest year ever, with 165 launches completed. At its current rate, the Falcon 9 is expected to fly just under 150 missions by the end of this year.
summary: SpaceX launched 27 Starlink Group 15-15 satellites from Vandenberg Space Force Base on a Falcon 9 rocket, with booster B1063 landing on a droneship for its 36th flight. This launch adds to a constellation of over 11,000 active spacecraft while SpaceX shifts focus to the Starship rocket, reducing Falcon 9 Starlink mission frequency.

title: Reprogramming Tumor Microenvironment May Boost Pancreatic Cancer Treatment Prospects
content:
Pancreatic cancer remains one of the most aggressive and difficult‑to‑treat cancers. Its resistance to therapy is largely attributed to a dense surrounding tissue that forms a protective barrier and suppresses the immune response. This barrier is a complex tumor microenvironment composed of supporting cells, blood vessels, and immune cells.

In pancreatic tumors, the microenvironment can account for up to 90 % of the tumor mass. Reprogramming this tissue has been suggested as a strategy that could improve prospects for effective treatment.

content:

Because aggressive treatment can cause significant side effects and lower quality of life, clinicians have struggled to identify which patients truly need intensive therapy. The test aims to better distinguish those who would benefit from stronger intervention from those who may do just as well with less aggressive care.

title: Bacteria Produce Powerful Antibiotics via Nonribosomal Peptide Synthetases
content:

NRPs are produced by large bacterial enzyme machineries called nonribosomal peptide synthetases, or NRPS for short. NRPS function like molecular assembly lines: similar to the stations in a car factory, where new parts are added to the car at each step, several specialized modules string together amino acid by amino acid to build a peptide.
summary: Bacteria produce many potent antibiotics, many of which are nonribosomal peptides (NRP). These NRP are assembled by large enzyme complexes called nonribosomal peptide synthetases (NRPS), which act like molecular assembly lines adding amino acids step by step.

title: MRC Lab creates dual‑color glowing plant reporters to track immune responses
content: Researchers at the MRC Laboratory of Medical Sciences have created a new method that improves the accuracy of glowing biological reporters. title: Corgi: A terminal multiplexer for managing multiple AI coding agents
content:

The design builds on the concept of Herdr, adding ergonomic features such as a live view of what each agent is doing and a continuous feed of their activity. A simple shortcut (F1) allows the user to jump to the next unread agent.

Corgi supports multiple accounts and includes a unified launcher for Codex, Claude Code, and Pi. It offers fast search and session resumption, inline usage tracking, and other small quality‑of‑life improvements for terminal use. Users can copy links with a single click, paste images with cmd+v (even over SSH), and view thumbnail previews of images. The tool also tracks CPU, memory, and GPU usage broken down by workspace.

The author created Corgi while on a frustrating sick leave, hoping it would help them return to work. They report mixed results but express satisfaction with the outcome and gratitude for the experience. A handful of friends have been using the tool for a few weeks and find it pleasant. The author acknowledges that there are still rough edges and invites feedback.
summary: Corgi is a terminal multiplexer designed to organize and monitor multiple AI agents, featuring a unified launcher for Codex, Claude Code, and Pi. It includes quality-of-life improvements such as image pasting, link copying, and built-in resource usage tracking.

title: Spotify to enforce QR code verification for Family and Duo plans
content:

The company’s support documentation confirms the policy, which gained attention after users on Reddit began reporting the new QR code prompts.

Users who fail to complete the QR code scan within seven days face significant consequences. Their accounts will be demoted to the free tier, and they will be prohibited from joining any other Duo or Family plan for a period of twelve months. While Spotify’s requirement that family plan members reside at the same address is a standard condition, the article notes that this enforcement may impact individuals in non-traditional living situations, such as children away at college or spouses who travel for work.

The increased verification efforts align with industry observations regarding plan sharing. A report by Goldman Sachs analysts, titled "Music in the Air: 10 Years On" and dated October 15, estimates that a significant portion of family plan users are friends sharing subscriptions to lower costs rather than actual household members. The analysts suggested that tightening household verification on multi-user plans presents additional monetization opportunities for the platform, noting that while most family plans require co-residence, practical enforcement has historically been minimal.
summary: Spotify is requiring users on Family and Duo plans to scan a QR code in person on the plan manager's device to maintain access. Failure to scan within seven days will demote the account to the free tier and bar the user from joining any other Duo or Family plan for 12 months.

The agency emphasized that this is the first time it has fully outlined the updated architecture, noting significant changes that had not been publicly disclosed before.

For SpaceX’s Starship, the new plan specifies that the Orion spacecraft will dock with the Starship lunar lander while in high‑Earth orbit. After docking, the combined vehicle will then transit to the Moon, marking a departure from earlier concepts that did not include a docking step.

Blue Origin’s architecture involves four launches of the New Glenn rocket and does not incorporate spacecraft‑to‑spacecraft refuelings. The plan also leaves open the possibility that Blue Origin’s Blue Moon lander could rendezvous with Orion in low‑lunar orbit, providing an additional option for lunar surface operations.
summary: NASA updates lander plans for Moon landings, finally solves long-festering Orion issue.

title: Under Fire by Humza Yousaf – a deeply affecting story of being stranded in Gaza
content:
Former Scottish First Minister Humza Yousaf has shared a personal account of his in-laws’ experience while stranded in Gaza during the conflict that began in 2023. According to Yousaf, a week after Israel’s bombing started following Hamas’s attack, his mother-in-law, Elizabeth, sent him a text message. In the message, she expressed fear for her life and asked him to promise to care for her daughters.

Elizabeth, a retired nurse from Dundee, and her Palestinian husband, Maged, were visiting family in Gaza when the bombing commenced. The couple became trapped in the region as the situation deteriorated. Yousaf notes that their home was filled with friends and neighbors whose houses had been destroyed, and they were running out of food. On the night Elizabeth sent the message, the group had been told to leave their neighborhood in Deir al-Balah due to impending strikes, though they later learned the evacuation order was a false alarm.

Yousaf describes the subsequent four weeks as a period of extreme distress, stating that the moment of receiving the text message felt like the lowest point for him. He characterizes the overall experience as a deeply affecting story of being stranded, highlighting the tragedy faced by those who were not as fortunate.
summary: Under Fire by Humza Yousaf – a deeply affecting story of being stranded in Gaza.

title: Murder on the dancefloor: are phones, drugs and chatter killing off dancing?
content:

She described her message as respectful, noting that while some conversation is acceptable, standing still in loud environments to discuss personal topics like new relationships or meals contradicts the purpose of a dancefloor.

content:

She recalled her first experience with reading at age four, when her father wrote the words from Fun With Dick and Jane on a chalkboard for her to memorize. Garmus described the moment of reading the book back to her father as feeling like magic, though she later discovered as an older child that the characters in the story did not actually have much fun.

Her favorite book growing up was Harriet the Spy by Louise Fitzhugh. The story follows eleven-year-old Harriet Welch, who aspires to be a writer and keeps a notebook to practice daily, encouraged by her nanny. When her classmates discover the notebook, which contains her meanest and most vulnerable thoughts, she becomes a pariah at school. Garmus stated that she read this story approximately a hundred times.

The character of Harriet Welch inspired Garmus to start writing things down. She also noted that the book taught her the importance of owning and apologizing for mistakes, regardless of how difficult it may feel.

title: Cheltenham's sharp novice hurdle winner at 20-1 marks Dawson's upset over Skelton
content:
The opening day of Cheltenham’s new season, the first since Gold Cup day in March, highlighted the enduring romance of jumps racing despite the sport’s increasing concentration of power among a few trainers. Dan Skelton, who defeated Willie Mullins to become the new champion over jumps last season, had already trained 115 winners in the current campaign before Friday’s racing. This total placed him nearly halfway toward Martin Pipe’s all-time record of 243 winners.

In contrast, trainer John Dawson had sent out a total of six winners from his North Yorkshire yard since May 2023. Dawson secured a victory in the Sharp Novices’ Hurdle, where an outsider won at 20-1 odds. This result served as a reminder that the winter code retains its romantic elements, even as the jumping game increasingly resembles the Flat in terms of the dominance held by a small number of top trainers.
summary: A 20-1 outsider won the Sharp Novices' Hurdle at the opening of Cheltenham's new season, marking a significant upset. Trainer John Dawson secured the victory over Dan Skelton, who had already trained 115 winners in the current campaign.

summary: Italian driver Kimi Antonelli has eight wins this season and his first drivers’ title is all but secure. At 20 years old and in only his second season, he could clinch the championship at this Sunday’s US Grand Prix in Austin or the next round in Mexico.

content:

title: Scientists uncover molecular pillars shaping cell mitochondria
content:

These powerpacks rely on a unique architecture consisting of two membranes, one nested inside the other, with a narrow gap between them known as the intermembrane space (IMS).

The organization of this tiny intermembrane space is critical to mitochondrial function, as it sustains the specific chemistry required for energy production.

title: NASA Tests RS-25 Engine No. 10001 at Stennis Space Center
content:
NASA teams at the Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, conducted a hot fire test of RS-25 engine No. 10001 on October 21, 2026. The test, documented by NASA photographer Danny Nowlin, lasted approximately 500 seconds, matching the duration of RS-25 engine firing during the launch of the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket. The engine operated at a 111% power level during the trial.

Each Artemis mission utilizes four RS-25 engines to generate up to 2 million pounds of combined thrust for the SLS rocket. All RS-25 engines are verified for flightworthiness at NASA Stennis before operational use. Although this specific developmental engine will not be deployed in a flight, the test enabled NASA and its prime contractor, L3Harris Technologies, to collect critical data aimed at enhancing engine performance and reliability.

title: Impossible Machines: Declarative Programming for the Physical World
content: Hey all — Sharing a thought experiment I put together. The premise: what might declarative programming feel like for the physical world? We’re already familiar with this paradigm in software land (eg SQL etc where we declare what we want and the execution engine figures out how). I didn’t have access to an actuator so I mocked up the concept in software. The way it works is you demonstrate the effect and the system figures out how to achieve it. So say you want to ring a bell and you have a crank. The system will find a way to connect the two. If you add obstacles it figures out how to work around them (runs a constraint solver runs behind the scenes). I think what’s interesting about this is being able to think about the problem at a higher level of abstraction, with the system figuring out a way to achieve the intended effect. Anyways, curious to read reactions, feedback, and interesting ideas on how to extend this! Comments URL: https://news. Ycombinator. Com/item? Id=50202746 Points: 36 # Comments: 7
summary: The developer presents a software simulation of declarative programming for the physical world, where users demonstrate a desired effect and the system determines how to achieve it. A constraint solver runs behind the scenes to find ways to connect actuators to effects while working around obstacles.
