title: US and Israel plan new strikes on Iran targeting energy sites, drones, missiles
content: Reports indicate that the United States and Israel have intensified military drills and are planning new strikes in Iran, potentially targeting energy sites, drone facilities and missile arsenals. The information comes from FRANCE 24’s correspondent in Jerusalem, Noga Tarnopolsky.
summary: Reports claim the US and Israel have increased military drills and planned new strikes in Iran. The strikes could target energy sites, drone facilities and missile arsenals, according to France 24 correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky.

title: Flavio Bolsonaro Leads Lula in Tight Brazil Runoff, Polls Narrow After Debate
content:
Brazil’s presidential future remains within the margin of error as the runoff approaches on Sunday. Recent polls consistently place far‑right candidate Flavio Bolsonaro ahead of left‑wing incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.

That lead has narrowed following last weekend’s acrimomious debate, tightening the race as the election draws closer.
summary: Most recent polls show far‑right Flavio Bolsonaro ahead of left‑wing incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in Brazil's upcoming presidential runoff. The margin narrowed after last weekend's acrimomious debate.
author: France 24

title: International Criminal Court receives EU's Sakharov Prize amid US sanctions
content:
The International Criminal Court was awarded the European Union’s top rights prize, the Sakharov Prize, on Thursday. Facing U.S. sanctions, the award could upset President Donald Trump.  

European Parliament chief Roberta Metsola said the EU is built on respect for multilateralism and international institutions, and that the prize recognises the court’s important work in upholding international law and justice.  

The ICC thanked the European Parliament for giving it the prize at a time when the Court and its officials face unprecedented challenges. FRANCE 24’s International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert has more.
summary: International Criminal Court receives EU's Sakharov Prize amid US sanctions.

title: Report says NHS waiting times for children in England sharply rising
content:
The Care Quality Commission’s annual State of Care report says thousands of children in England are facing some of the sharpest increases in NHS waiting times ever recorded. The research links the long delays to harder‑to‑treat conditions and notes regional differences in the level of care provided.

While the report indicates that waiting times for some adult services have improved, it adds that children and young people are being “hit hardest” as demand rises and staff numbers fall.
summary: Report says NHS waiting times for children in England sharply rising.

title: King Charles urged as ‘human brother’ to back Caribbean reparations talks at CHOGM
content: Caricom commission chair Hilary Beckles wants king to ensure Commonwealth becomes a ‘moral institution committed to human justice’ The head of the Caribbean’s reparations commission has appealed to King Charles III as a “human brother” whose family he said had benefited from slavery to support reparations talks at next month’s Commonwealth leaders meeting in the Caribbean. Speaking at a press conference ahead of the Commonwealth heads of government meeting ( Chogm ) in Antigua and Barbuda next month, professor Hilary Beckles urged the king to use his influence to advance slavery reparations talks between Britain and the Caribbean.
summary: Professor Hilary Beckles, chair of the CARICOM reparations commission, appealed to King Charles III as a “human brother” whose family benefited from slavery. He urged the king to use his influence to support slavery reparations talks at the Commonwealth heads of government meeting in Antigua and Barbuda.

title: 150,000 Student List supporters rally in Belgrade ahead of Serbian election
content:
About 150,000 supporters of the Student List movement gathered in central Belgrade on Thursday, marching in a large rally ahead of the parliamentary elections scheduled for the weekend.

The Student List, described as a leaderless movement of student‑backed candidates, says it aims to oust the party of veteran leader Aleksandar Vucic, the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), and end more than 14 years of its rule in the Sunday vote.
summary: About 150,000 supporters of the opposition Student List movement rallied in central Belgrade on Thursday. The rally called for ousting veteran leader Aleksandar Vucic’s Serbian Progressive party in the parliamentary elections this weekend.
author: Guardian World

title: Rebel Wilson wins Australian court case, co‑producers receive $10
content: A New South Wales Supreme Court judge dismissed the lawsuit filed by the co‑producers of The Deb and awarded Australian actress Rebel Wilson almost $400,000 after she countersued. The court awarded the co‑producers a token sum of $10. Wilson, who directed, co‑produced and starred in the musical‑comedy debut film, faced accusations from the co‑producers of sabotage, lying and contract breaches. The case marks another Australian court victory for Wilson amid a series of legal disputes surrounding the film in both Australia and the United States.
summary: A NSW Supreme Court judge dismissed the case brought by the co‑producers of The Deb and awarded Rebel Wilson almost $400,000. The co‑producers were awarded only $10 after the star countersued.

title: Australia offers astronaut Katherine Bennell-Pegg a 2028 ISS mission
content:
Australian of the Year Katherine Bennell‑Pegg has been offered a seat on a 2028 International Space Station mission. The Australian federal government has formally presented an invitation to the European Space Agency (ESA) to include Bennell‑Pegg in the crew.  

If the offer is accepted, Bennell‑Pegg would become the first qualified astronaut to fly to space under the Australian flag. The 2028 mission would therefore mark a historic first for Australia in terms of flag‑qualified spaceflight.
summary: The Australian federal government has offered the European Space Agency to send astronaut Katherine Bennell-Pegg, the Australian of the Year, to the International Space Station. If the 2028 mission proceeds, she would be the first astronaut to fly under the Australian flag.
author: Guardian World

title: After Starshield interruption, Ukraine wants to build its own satellite communication network with ICEYE and Nokia
content:
Ukraine has signed a letter of intent with Finnish telecommunications company Nokia and satellite manufacturer ICEYE to explore the development of a sovereign satellite-communications network. The agreement, announced on October 22, aims to establish secure, high-performance satellite systems that Ukraine fully controls. Rafal Modrzewski, ICEYE’s cofounder and CEO, stated that the company has a proven track record of delivering sovereign missions and has supported Ukraine since 2022. He emphasized the need for Ukraine to possess communications infrastructure it can rely on independently.

The move comes in response to recent disruptions in Ukraine’s access to existing satellite services. Ukraine currently relies heavily on SpaceX’s Starlink megaconstellation and Starshield, a military-grade version of Starlink used by the U.S. Government and its allies. Starshield is particularly crucial for Ukraine, as it enables the operation of fast-moving drones over large distances in both offensive and defensive capacities. On October 14, Ukrainian soldiers and officials reported a severe throttling of Starshield services, which imposed speed limits on terminal-carrying drones and caused many to crash.

Responsibility for the throttling remains unclear. Some U.S. officials indicated the order came from Elon Musk, but Musk stated that Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the U.S. government. In a post on X on October 14, Musk asserted that any limits on speed or usage are decided by the U.S. military and ultimately the President. The throttling appears to still be in effect, reinforcing Ukraine’s desire to control its own satellite-communications infrastructure.

Mikko Hautala, Nokia’s chief geopolitical and government relations officer and chairman of Nokia Defense, noted that satellite networks are key to secure communications when ground networks are disrupted. He stated that through the letter of intent, Nokia, Ukraine, and ICEYE will explore how trusted, sovereign satellite communications can strengthen Ukraine’s resilience. This partnership builds on an agreement announced on October 1 between Nokia and ICEYE to help nations develop similar sovereign systems.

ICEYE already supports the Ukrainian defense effort through its fleet of Earth-observing satellites in low Earth orbit, which use synthetic aperture radar. Ukraine utilizes data from the ICEYE constellation for intelligence and planning. This relationship has placed ICEYE in a vulnerable position, as a Russian inspector satellite named Kosmos 2612 recently made an extremely close approach to ICEYE-X36, a satellite operated by ICEYE US. The goal of this unsanctioned rendezvous is unclear, though it may have been intended to assess capabilities, interfere with the satellite, or send a message regarding Russia’s ability to interact with satellites.
summary: Ukraine wants its own satellite-communication system, which shouldn't be surprising given the events of the past week or so. The Ukrainian military just signed a letter of intent with two Finnish companies — the telecom giant Nokia and satellite maker ICEYE — to look into developing a sovereign satellite-communications network for Ukraine.

title: Space Shuttle Columbia carries Gene Roddenberry's ashes into space on STS-52
content: On Oct. 22, 1992, the space shuttle Columbia launched into space with the ashes of Gene Roddenberry, the creator of " Star Trek," aboard. During mission STS-52, NASA astronaut and shuttle commander James Wetherbee brought a small container with a portion of Roddenberry's ashes into space as part of his personal effects at the request of Roddenberry's widow, Majel Barrett. It was Roddenberry's lifelong dream to go to space, but he never got to go while he was alive. But thanks to his wife, a little bit of Roddenberry finally made it to space almost exactly one year after his death. NASA and his family didn't tell anyone about it until almost two years later in 1994. Wetherbee said he was "honored to be asked" by Barrett to carry Roddenberry's ashses on the spaceflight. "I'm just glad I was able to bring a little happiness to the family," he said, according to Newsweek. The Space Shuttle Columbia (STS-52) launches from NASA's Kennedy Space Center on Oct. 22, 1992. (Image credit: NASA) Here's why it mattered The launch of Roddenberry's ashes into space on NASA's STS-52 mission aboard the space shuttle Columbia marked the world's first " space burial," but it wouldn't be the last. About five years after Roddenberry's memorial flight, in 1997, the space memorial company Celestis began launching a series of "burial" flights by flying capsules with human cremains on rockets. In fact, more of Roddenberry's ashes flew on Celestis' "founders flight" in April 1997 aboard an air-launched Pegasus rocket that took off from the Canary Islands in Spain. The ashes of Roddenberry's wife and of Star Trek actor James Dooha n have also flown in space, among others. Celestis has gone on to launch human cremains on many suborbital and orbital flights, including some on SpaceX Falcon 9 rockets. The company even launched the ashes of the late astronomer Eugene Shoemaker to the moon in 1999 on the Luna 1 flight, with another set of cremains launched into deep space on the Enterprise mission in 2023. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.
summary: On Oct. 22, 1992, NASA shuttle Columbia on mission STS-52 carried a small container of Gene Roddenberry’s ashes into space. The ashes were placed aboard at the request of his widow Majel Barrett and were later disclosed in 1994, marking the first space burial.

title: Europe's Space Rider vehicle comes crashing down during drop test
content:
On October 6, the European Space Agency (ESA) conducted a full-scale drop test of its Space Rider prototype at a military range on the Italian island of Sardinia. The minivan-sized mockup was released from a helicopter at an altitude of approximately 2 miles (3 kilometers) to evaluate the vehicle’s descent and landing systems. While the initial drogue parachute deployed successfully and began slowing the descent, the main steerable parafoil detached during its deployment sequence. This anomaly left the prototype unable to slow its descent further, resulting in a crash into the ground.

The failure occurred during a system-level test intended to demonstrate Space Rider’s ability to perform runway-style touchdowns using its wingless, lifting-body design. According to an ESA spokesperson, the test was not completed as planned due to the issue with the parafoil. An independent investigation is currently ongoing to determine the root cause of the failure and to inform the next steps in the development process. ESA officials confirmed that all components of the craft have been recovered following the incident.

Géraldine Naja, ESA’s director of space transportation, addressed the event during an ESA Council media briefing on October 22. She described the incident as an unfortunate but important part of space system development, noting that many successful tests had preceded this attempt. Naja stated that the remaining qualification activities for Space Rider are not on the critical path of the vehicle’s development. Consequently, she expressed hope that this specific test failure would not damage or require modifications to the remaining schedule and qualification activities.

Space Rider is being developed as Europe’s first reusable, uncrewed orbital spacecraft, designed to carry scientific experiments to orbit for up to two months before returning them to Earth. Its unique landing method relies on a steerable parachute to maneuver toward a landing area, distinguishing it from other current spacecraft recovery practices. The descent and landing qualification campaign began in 2025, with previous successes demonstrating the vehicle’s autonomous capabilities and parafoil deployment.

The October 6 test was the first drop test since an unsuccessful attempt in May, when a sensor flagged an issue during preparations, leading engineers to abort the test before release. Following that incident, the testing range operated by Italy’s Ministry of Defense was unavailable from June through September. Beyond landing systems, Space Rider underwent separate thermal protection testing earlier in the year, where heat-shield materials were exposed to temperatures around 2,900 degrees Fahrenheit (1,600 degrees Celsius) in plasma wind tunnel trials. ESA has targeted the vehicle’s first orbital mission for later this decade.
summary: Europe's Space Rider vehicle comes crashing down during drop test.
author: Space.com

title: Billy Evans emerges as key villain in Elizabeth Holmes documentary
content:
Nathan Fielder’s documentary You Can See Everything has emerged as a surprise hit, featuring Elizabeth Holmes, the Theranos founder currently serving a prison sentence for defrauding investors. The film also showcases Fielder, known for his comedy-reality series Nathan for You and The Rehearsal, as an on-camera co-director. While audiences are likely familiar with Holmes from her media coverage and the Hulu miniseries The Dropout, a third figure, Billy Evans, plays a significant role in the second half of the film.

Evans, Holmes’s partner, is described as a not-particularly-famous individual whose screen time competes with the three well-known faces in what is characterized as a four-character drama. Holmes has stated that she and Evans are not legally married, though they became engaged in 2018, have two children, and treat each other as spouses. Despite his lower profile, Evans is not excluded from the narrative in terms of screen time or memorability.

However, Evans remains the odd man out in the broader discourse surrounding the film. As You Can See Everything sparks conversations about manipulation, shifting sympathies, and trust, a consensus has formed among viewers regarding Evans. The source notes that in all the discussion prompted by the movie, everyone seems to agree on one crucial point: Billy Evans sucks. This reaction highlights how the film’s portrayal of Evans has become a focal point for audience engagement, distinguishing him from the other central figures in the documentary.
summary: Nathan Fielder’s documentary You Can See Everything identifies Elizabeth Holmes’s partner Billy Evans as a central figure in the film’s narrative. The article notes that viewers widely agree Evans is the film’s most untrustworthy character despite his lower public profile.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Cathinka Tandberg: ‘Spurs fans hate Arsenal. That’s how it is’
content: Norwegian forward might look to Harry Kane for inspiration on the pitch, but when north London derby comes around, she needs no lessons on what the rivalry means “It means more than just three points. It’s for the whole club. It’s for the whole place. It’s for the whole of Tottenham.” One only needs to be in the presence of Tottenham Hotspur’s Cathinka Tandberg for a few minutes to feel the passion that emanates from her when it comes to this weekend’s north London derby. As a lifelong Spurs fan, the forward understands more than most the intensity of the rivalry that exists between her side and Arsenal, one that she cannot wait to experience once again on Saturday. “It will just be an incredible feeling,” she tells Moving the Goalposts. “I think you will feel a few nerves that you maybe don’t feel in a normal game but that’s good.”
summary: Cathinka Tandberg: ‘Spurs fans hate Arsenal. That’s how it is’.

content:

title: Trump declines to confirm if he called Musk to restore Starlink for Ukraine
content: President Trump declined on Thursday to confirm whether he personally contacted SpaceX founder Elon Musk to restore Starlink services for Ukraine. Speaking to reporters before leaving the White House, the President stated, “I don’t want to say, but I know it was a very interesting situation,” adding that he did not wish to comment one way or the other.
summary: President Trump refused to state whether he contacted SpaceX founder Elon Musk to restore Starlink for Ukraine. He described the situation as interesting but declined to comment further before leaving the White House.
